subject: Pediatrics
question: A newborn is delivered at 42 weeks of gestation. On examination, the baby has dry, peeling skin, long fingernails and toenails, abundant hair on scalp, meconium-stained skin. Which of the following conditions does this neonate most likely have?
explanation: A baby delivered at 42 weeks of gestation or later is considered post-term. The classic features described - dry, cracking, peeling skin, long fingernails, and meconium staining - are hallmarks of Post-maturity syndrome. This condition results from the placenta aging and losing function, leading to fetal undernourishment and skin breakdown in the amniotic fluid.
